checkpoints: Problem 1 — caching node_modules directly is risky because many packages contain native modules (binaries precompiled for a specific OS/CPU architecture).

Consequence of Problem 1 — if the runner image version changes or the job runs on a different runner type, the restored node_modules may be incompatible, causing a confusing module-load error instead of a clean cache miss.

Fix for Problem 1 — cache ~/.npm (npm's download cache of tarballs, not compiled binaries) instead of node_modules, then let npm ci rebuild node_modules; this is still significantly faster than a full reinstall since the network-download step is cached, while native-module compilation always runs correctly for the current environment.
Problem 2 — using a static key like node-modules-cache means every run gets a cache hit against the same entry regardless of whether package-lock.json changed, so the key never invalidates.

Consequence of Problem 2 — when a dependency is added, removed, or upgraded, the job still runs against stale, wrong dependencies, potentially hiding a fixed bug or running a version with a vulnerability already patched in the newer lockfile.

Fix for Problem 2 — key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}, following the core principle that a good cache key must be a function of exactly what determines the cache's content (the lockfile, not the application source), so the hash changes exactly when a reinstall is needed.
Optional enhancement — add restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-npm- as a fallback prefix so a near/partial match can be picked up when there's no exact key match, instead of a total cache miss.
Root cause: the `docker buildx build ... --push .` command has no `--cache-from`/`--cache-to` parameters at all, so buildx defaults to the local cache backend.
Local cache is stored on the filesystem of the exact runner that performed that specific build — it is not portable across machines.

GitHub Actions runners are ephemeral: GitHub provisions a fresh, clean VM for each job and destroys it right after the job finishes, so the local cache from one build disappears with its runner, and each subsequent build job starts on a different, empty-filesystem runner with nothing to reuse — this is why the log never shows a single `CACHED` line no matter how many times it's rebuilt on the same branch.
This is explicitly not a Dockerfile layer-ordering problem, since layer order only matters when a single persistent cache exists across builds to compare against and reuse.

Fix: switch to a registry cache backend by adding both `--cache-to type=registry,ref=...,mode=max` and `--cache-from type=registry,ref=...`, pointing at a dedicated cache tag on the container registry.

`mode=max` on `--cache-to` pushes all intermediate layers, including intermediate build stages (not just the final layer), to that registry cache tag after every build, while `--cache-from` pulls that cache back down at the start of the next build.
Because the registry exists independently of any runner, this cache survives every runner being destroyed and recreated, so subsequent builds show `CACHED` lines for unchanged layers.
As a result, build time drops from ~8 minutes to a few dozen seconds.
Principal type là `Federated`, `identifiers` trỏ đúng `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github.arn` (ARN của OIDC provider GitHub đã tồn tại) — không phải `AWS` hay ARN role/user khác
Action đúng là `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` — action riêng cho luồng web-identity federation, không phải `sts:AssumeRole` thường
Có condition `StringEquals` trên biến `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud` với value `sts.amazonaws.com`, xác nhận token GitHub phát ra thực sự nhắm tới audience AWS STS
Có condition riêng trên biến `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub`, và operator dùng là `StringEquals` — KHÔNG phải `StringLike` hay bất kỳ dạng wildcard/pattern-match nào

Value của condition `sub` là chuỗi CHÍNH XÁC VÀ ĐẦY ĐỦ `repo:my-org/my-app:ref:refs/heads/main`, đúng format `repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:<full-ref>` — không được rút gọn thành mức repo (vd `repo:my-org/my-app:*`) hay bỏ phần `ref:refs/heads/main`

Hai condition `aud` và `sub` nằm trong CÙNG một `statement` block duy nhất (một `effect = "Allow"`), không tách thành hai statement Allow riêng biệt — tách riêng sẽ biến logic AND (bắt buộc thoả cả hai) thành OR, phá vỡ mục đích siết chặt

`assume_role_policy` của `aws_iam_role` được gán bằng `data.aws_iam_policy_document.<tên>.json` — chính policy document vừa định nghĩa được dùng làm trust policy thật cho role, không phải một policy JSON khác hay bỏ trống

Issue 1a (most severe) — the trust policy's `StringLike` condition on `sub` never pins a `ref`, so a token minted from any branch of a matching repo (not just `refs/heads/main`) satisfies the condition and can assume the role.

Issue 1b (most severe) — the same condition uses `repo:my-org/*` at the repo level, so any repository in the `my-org` organization — not just `my-app` — can produce a token matching the condition and assume the AWS deploy role.

Issue 2 — unsafe action pinning: `some-3rd-party/deploy-action@main` references the mutable `main` branch, so if that action's repo is compromised, the next workflow run executes the malicious code at the exact step that already holds the AWS OIDC credential.

Issue 3 — branch protection missing required status checks: `github_branch_protection` only enforces `required_pull_request_reviews` (1 approval) with no `required_status_checks`, letting a PR merge into `main` without any CI, test, or security scan ever passing.

Compounding attack path: a PR that skipped all status checks (issue 3) gets approved and merged, triggering `deploy.yaml`, which runs the possibly-compromised `deploy-action@main` (issue 2), under AWS permissions that the whole org — not just `my-app` on `main` — can assume (issue 1a/1b), giving a full org-to-production-AWS attack path with no sophisticated exploit needed.
Fix for issue 1: change the trust policy to `StringEquals` with `repo:my-org/my-app:ref:refs/heads/main` (pins both repo and branch) plus an `aud = sts.amazonaws.com` condition.
Fix for issue 2: pin `deploy-action` to a full commit SHA instead of `@main`.
Fix for issue 3: add `required_status_checks { contexts = ["ci", "security-scan"] strict = true }` to `github_branch_protection` so CI/scans must pass before merging into `main`.

Problem 1 root cause: `minRunners = maxRunners = 5` forces the ARC flotilla to keep exactly 5 runner pods alive 24/7 with zero ability to scale to zero, which is what causes the ~70% wasted idle-time cost.

Problem 1 fix: set `minRunners = 0` (keep `maxRunners` as-is, e.g. 5, for peak capacity) so the flotilla shrinks to 0 pods when the job queue is empty and scales up to `maxRunners` when jobs arrive — true scale-to-zero autoscaling.

Trade-off of `minRunners = 0`: the first job after an idle period incurs a pod cold-start delay (seconds to a minute), which is an acceptable cost versus saving most of the compute spend during idle time.
Problem 2 root cause (missing cache): the workflow's dependency-install step is a bare `npm ci` with no `actions/cache` step at all, so nothing about the install is ever cached.

Problem 2 root cause (ephemeral runners): ARC runner pods are ephemeral — destroyed right after each job — so nothing persists between runs, meaning `npm ci` re-downloads every dependency from scratch each time even when `package-lock.json` is unchanged.

Problem 2 fix: add an `actions/cache@v4` step before `npm ci`, caching `~/.npm` (not `node_modules`, to avoid non-portable native module issues across builds/runners) keyed by `hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')` with a `restore-keys` fallback — the cache hits when the lockfile is unchanged and auto-invalidates when it changes.
The two fixes are independent but complementary: `minRunners = 0` solves the idle-time cost waste, while dependency caching solves the per-run build speed problem.
Không hoàn toàn đồng ý với nhận định rằng Jenkinsfile chỉ là Groovy tự do, không cần phân biệt Declarative/Scripted.
Declarative Pipeline có cấu trúc cố định `pipeline { agent; stages; steps; post }`, cấu trúc này cho phép Jenkins validate syntax ngay từ đầu.
Declarative đi kèm các building block khai báo sẵn như `when`/`post`/`parallel`.
Scripted Pipeline là Groovy thuần (`node { stage('x') { ... } }`), thực sự linh hoạt hơn cho vòng lặp tùy ý và logic phức tạp.
Đánh đổi của sự linh hoạt ở Scripted: khó đọc hơn, khó review trong PR hơn, và dễ để script phình to đến mức không ai dám đụng vào.
Mặc định dùng Declarative cho khoảng 90% trường hợp.
Chỉ hạ xuống Scripted qua khối `script { }` lồng bên trong Declarative, khi có logic động thực sự không thể biểu đạt bằng khai báo (ví dụ: tính tên artifact từ nhiều điều kiện cùng lúc).

Rủi ro cần lưu ý: sự tự do của Scripted dễ khiến gọi nhầm một Groovy method ngoài sandbox allowlist gây ra `RejectedAccessException`, rủi ro mà Declarative giảm bớt vì các step tích hợp sẵn đã được pre-approved.
Freestyle jobs live entirely in the UI (config.xml stored on the controller), so changes aren't version-controlled and can't be reviewed via a pull request.
Freestyle jobs are lost entirely if the Jenkins controller dies, since their definition has no source of truth outside controller-local state.

Step 1: rewrite each existing build step across the 5 Freestyle jobs as a declarative Jenkinsfile (pipeline { agent; stages; steps; post }) stored next to the source code in the repo, with each old build step becoming a matching stage/steps block.

Step 2: use the Terraform provider taiidani/jenkins to declare jenkins_job with a template that renders a CpsScmFlowDefinition config.xml, so the job only points at the Jenkinsfile in SCM (Git) instead of a loose script typed in the UI.

Step 3: move every credential the job uses (token, password) out of manually-typed UI fields into jenkins_credential_username declared in Terraform, scoped inside a jenkins_folder, to avoid secrets scattered with no control.
Run terraform plan to review changes before the real apply, then after apply run a second plan that must show 'No changes' to confirm the job is truly idempotent (real job-as-code).
Going forward, every job change goes through Terraform + PR review instead of manual UI edits.
A periodic terraform plan catches any accidental UI drift and pulls the job definition back in line with the code.
Explicitly answers 'No' — states stash/unstash and archiveArtifacts are NOT interchangeable because they serve different purposes for the two needs described

Identifies `stash`/`unstash` as the mechanism to pass the binary from Build to the parallel Unit/Lint branches (e.g. `stash name: 'bin', ...` right after Build, `unstash 'bin'` at the start of each branch)
Identifies `archiveArtifacts` (typically in the `post` block) as the mechanism to persist the binary so it stays attached to the build and downloadable from the Jenkins UI weeks later
Explains stash is temporary and build-scoped — it is cleaned up once the build run ends, which is why it cannot serve the weeks-later release-download need
Explains archiveArtifacts is the wrong/slow model for passing data between parallel branches during the same build (not built for fast inter-branch reuse)
Notes that because each parallel branch (Unit, Lint) has its own separate workspace/executor, each branch must call unstash itself rather than automatically seeing the binary
Notes Unit and Lint run concurrently on separate executors, so total Test-stage time is roughly max(Unit, Lint) rather than their sum

Investigate by opening the full console log first and checking whether the Deploy stage is mentioned at all — looking for an explicit skip message (e.g. "Stage Deploy skipped due to when conditional") as a clue, rather than assuming the job is simply broken.
Add a temporary diagnostic echo at the top of the pipeline printing env.BRANCH_NAME and env.GIT_BRANCH, then re-run the build to see their actual values.

Identify the root mechanism: `when { branch 'main' }` is designed for a Multibranch Pipeline (where Jenkins auto-sets env.BRANCH_NAME per discovered branch), but a single, non-Multibranch Pipeline job pointing at a fixed Jenkinsfile may leave env.BRANCH_NAME empty/unset, so the condition silently fails to match.
Recognize that a `when` condition that fails to match causes Jenkins to SKIP the stage entirely rather than fail it — no error is ever recorded for the Deploy stage.
Explain why nobody notices: a silently skipped stage produces no visible error, so the overall build still reports SUCCESS/green.

Fix the condition based on the diagnostic evidence (BRANCH_NAME empty, GIT_BRANCH holding 'origin/main') by changing it to `when { expression { env.GIT_BRANCH == 'origin/main' } }` to match the variable the job actually sets.
Propose a long-term safeguard: add a branch-logging line to the first stage of every Jenkinsfile so a silent stage-skip surfaces directly in the log in the future.

Correctly ranks the hardcoded `REGISTRY_TOKEN = 'glpat-...'` literal in `environment` as the most severe issue, because it gets committed permanently into git history and stays readable to anyone with repo access even after the token is rotated.

Proposes fixing it by storing the token as a Jenkins credential (e.g. a Secret text credential via Terraform `jenkins_credential_username` or the equivalent secret-text resource) and injecting it through `withCredentials([string(credentialsId: 'registry-token', variable: 'REGISTRY_TOKEN')])` instead of a literal value in the Jenkinsfile.

Identifies the second issue and its concrete manifestation together: Jenkins credential masking only redacts secret values in the console log (not when the pipeline writes them to a file), and the `echo "Deployed with token ${REGISTRY_TOKEN}" > out/deploy-log.txt` line combined with `archiveArtifacts` exposes the raw token in a downloadable UI artifact, bypassing masking entirely.
Proposes fixing it by removing the line that writes the token to a file, and only logging non-secret info such as `BUILD_NUMBER` and a timestamp if a deploy log is needed.
Identifies the third issue: `agent any` lets the stage run directly on the Jenkins controller, letting even an untrusted PR build read `JENKINS_HOME` and other controller-level secrets.
Proposes fixing it by setting `numExecutors: 0` on the controller and specifying `agent { label 'deploy' }` instead of `any`, forcing the build onto an isolated agent.
